## Function

GDNF is a secreted trophic ligand best known for supporting neuronal survival and development through GFRα co-receptors and RET signaling. It is especially relevant to the enteric nervous system, while stromal, neural, epithelial, and tumour contexts can respond differently.

::: {.gene-mechanism}
::: {.gene-state}
**GDNF signaling available**

Supports survival, differentiation, and tissue–nerve communication in suitable receptor-bearing cells.
:::
::: {.gene-flow-arrow}
→
:::
::: {.gene-state .gene-state-off}
**GDNF reduced**

Trophic support may decline; the phenotype depends on which cell supplied and received the signal.
:::
:::

Promoter methylation in UC-associated literature is interesting, but “GDNF off” cannot be translated into one universal cancer effect. RET signaling can be beneficial in normal development yet co-opted in malignancy.

<details><summary><strong>Resolve the signaling circuit</strong></summary>

Measure ligand source, GFRA/RET receptor expression, phospho-RET pathway activity, spatial context, and methylation–expression coupling.
</details>
